'''Graador''' was a [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] that featured [[Cave/Legends|caverns]] large enough to fit entire [[Fleet/Legends|fleets]] of [[Starship/Legends|starships]] in them. The caverns were [[Homeworld/Legends|home]] to both immense [[Exogorth/Legends|exogorths]] and [[Mynock/Legends|mynocks]] that could survive in the planet's [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. Graador was also inhabited by two [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]]: the [[Farmer/Legends|agrarian]] [[Graadorian]]s and a [[Mutant mynock|mutated type]] of intelligent mynocks.

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a group of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] agents [[Mission to Graador|surveyed]] Graador's caverns, which they initially deemed a suitable location for a new Rebel base and the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]]. However, after making contact with the local exogorths and sentient mynocks who intended to [[Diet/Legends|feed]] on the Rebels' starships and [[Power generator/Legends|power generators]], respectively, the agents were forced to evade members of both species until the fleet could be warned of the threat posed to it by Graador's inhabitants.

==Description==
Graador was a remote terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="RECG" /> located in the [[Graador system/Legends|Graador system]], a part of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim's]] [[Graador sector/Legends|Graador sector]].<ref name="EAOC" /> It featured several immense [[Cave/Legends|caverns]] inside which multiple [[Fleet/Legends|fleets]] of [[Starship/Legends|starships]] could easily fit.<ref name="RECG" />

The caverns of Graador were home to a large population of a variant of the [[Mynock/Legends|mynock]]<ref name="RECG" />&mdash;a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Diet/Legends|ergovorous]] creature that,<ref name="CSWE mynock">{{CSWECite|II|347|mynock}}</ref> although presumed to have [[Homeworld/Legends|originated]] from the<ref name="CSWE Ord Mynock">{{CSWECite|II|420|Ord Mynock}}</ref> [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]<ref name="EAOC Mynock">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Mynockra system]]</ref> planet [[Ord Mynock/Legends|Ord Mynock]],<ref name="CSWE Ord Mynock" /> usually inhabited the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of outer [[Realspace/Legends|space]] and for whom planetary [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheres]] frequently were [[Death/Legends|lethal]].<ref name="CSWE mynock" /> The Graador type of mynocks, however, could tolerate the world's air, and they shared their habitat with colossal [[Exogorth/Legends|exogorths]],<ref name="RECG" /> which were also typically well-adapted for the rigors of living in space.<ref name="CSWE space slug">{{CSWECite|III|181|space slug (exogorth)}}</ref>

==History==
{{RPGseed}}
[[File:Mynock_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Rebel Alliance agents encountered both non-sentient and intelligent mynocks (pictured) on Graador.]]
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a group of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] agents were tasked with finding a suitable location for a new main Alliance base in the wake of the [[Evacuation of Yavin|evacuation]] of the [[Great Temple/Legends|facility]] on the<ref name="RECG" /> Outer Rim Territories [[Moon/Legends|moon]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. Following several unsuccessful attempts, the Rebel [[General/Legends|General]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]] [[Mission to Graador|dispatched]] the team to Graador.<ref name="RECG" />

There, the Rebels deemed that the planet's caves could be adapted for use both by Rebel personnel and the entire [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]]. The team also discovered the native population of non-sentient mynocks but considered them to be merely a minor nuisance. The creatures did, however, consume the agents' [[Subspace transceiver/Legends|transceiver]] equipment after they had contacted Cracken to tell him that the Rebel fleet could be brought to Graador.<ref name="RECG" />

The group of Rebels subsequently came into contact with both the planet's exogorths and the [[Mutant mynock|group]] of [[Mutant|mutated]], [[Sentience/Legends|intelligent]] mynocks that controlled them, discovering that the latter intended to feed on the Rebels' [[Power generator/Legends|power generators]] while letting their enthralled exogorths consume the Alliance starships. When the Rebel agents killed several of the mutant mynocks, the exogorths went on a rampage, and the team was forced to evade both them and the rest of the mynocks until the agents' [[Communications array/Legends|communications array]] could be repaired and used to warn the Alliance Fleet of the trap that awaited it at Graador.<ref name="RECG" />
{{Endgame}}

==Inhabitants==
Overall, Graador offered little beyond basic sustenance to living beings on it, which included the [[Farmer/Legends|agrarian]] [[Graadorian]]s. Other natives of Graador included a type of mynocks that had mutated and evolved sentience. The intelligent mynocks possessed the means to control the exogorths that lived on Graador.<ref name="RECG" />

==Behind the scenes==
Graador was introduced in the [[2009]] sourcebook ''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]'', which was published by [[Wizards of the Coast]] for use with the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''. In the book, the planet serves as the setting for a [[roleplaying game]] adventure hook that this article assumes plays out as described.<ref name="RECG" /> The [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]] to the 2009 reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Graador [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore Graador, in grid square I-17.<ref name="EAOC" />
